note: The closest match to the stated ICP in this batch, and close enough that he nearly restates it himself. On neglected health his words track the ICP quote almost exactly: 'the rest of my life is going well, there's some extra success and all that stuff in my career, my personal life goes very well for me in a bunch of different areas. This is the one area where I've just accepted, I continue to make excuses for myself.' Successful and high-earning: a sales professional travelling internationally with client meetings booked across breakfast, lunch and dinner, who says 'I'm doing well' and places $6,000 as 'not a large amount of money'. Good-to-great is explicit — he rates his shape 5 out of 10, says 'I'm not like in terrible shape, thankfully I've aged well', and 'I don't want to be mediocre'. And plainly not deconditioned: a lifelong athlete who still boxes, spars and does mitt work at a private gym. The finding worth carrying forward is that this perfect-fit prospect did not buy, and not on price. He hesitated on proof and on method comparison — a stranger asking for thousands one day after he first saw a video, with no materials to evaluate. If the stated ICP is right about who the customer is, then the loss here is a sales-asset problem rather than a targeting problem, and it is the mirror image of the existing Robyn Stillwater assessment where someone outside the ICP closed at full price.
